summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the invalidators of wudu and addresses a nuanced jurisprudential question: what should a person do when they have partial access to water but cannot use it on certain parts of their body due to injury, illness, or a cast? Sh. Ali Mashhour explains the two main scholarly approaches—one permitting combined use of wudu and tayammum (the weaker opinion), and another (the majority view) holding that wudu and tayammum are complete alternatives never used together. According to the stronger opinion that Sh. Ali Mashhour presents, a person performs wudu to the extent possible, wipes over parts they cannot wash (following the precedent of wiping over footwear and turbans), and does not resort to tayammum. Sh. Ali Mashhour concludes by addressing whether tayammum can be performed on surfaces beyond earth, such as painted walls, confirming that any surface on which dust can settle qualifies as valid for tayammum.
